# Copilot instructions — Min Hero Calc

Offline-first PWA calculator for *Min Hero: Tower of Sages*: team composition, type
coverage, and skill builds. Vanilla TypeScript, no UI framework, no runtime
dependencies — all data ships inside the bundle.

## Setup, build, check

```powershell
npm.cmd i                # installs the declared devDependencies
npm.cmd run dev          # vite dev server
npm.cmd run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
npm.cmd run test         # vitest run (tests/**/*.test.ts, node environment)
npm.cmd run data:import  # regenerate the data pack from local decompiled source
npm.cmd run data:check   # validate generated data (tests/data.test.ts)
npm.cmd run assets:import # copy sprites, move icons, gem/UI art into public/assets
npm.cmd run assets:check # verify the asset manifest against public/assets
npm.cmd run build        # prebuild regenerates icons, then tsc && vite build
npm.cmd run preview      # serve the production build
npm.cmd run verify       # typecheck + tests
npm.cmd run icons        # regenerate public/icons/icon-{192,512}.png (plain Node)

# installable packs (see "Download builds")
npm.cmd run desktop:install  # one-off Electron toolchain install
npm.cmd run desktop:app      # -> desktop/release/*.exe
npm.cmd run desktop:smoke    # headless boot check of the packaged app
npm.cmd run android:icons    # -> assets/*.png + android res via @capacitor/assets
npm.cmd run android:apk      # -> release/MinHeroCalc-<version>.apk
```

- `vite`, `vite-plugin-pwa`, `typescript` and `vitest` are declared in
  `devDependencies`; commit `package-lock.json` so installs are reproducible.
- In PowerShell on this machine `npm.ps1` is blocked by execution policy; call
  `npm.cmd` instead.
- Vitest is configured in `vitest.config.ts` and uses the Node environment. There
  is still no linter; run `typecheck` and `test` after changes.
- `tsconfig.json` includes `src` and `tests`, and enables `resolveJsonModule` for
  the upcoming data pack. `vite.config.ts`/`vitest.config.ts` are not typechecked
  by the script — verify config edits by running a build/test.
- **Every script must run on Linux.** `prebuild` regenerates the PWA icons via
  `scripts/make-icons.mjs` (hand-rasterised shapes + `node:zlib`, no image
  tooling). It replaced a PowerShell/System.Drawing script that broke Cloudflare
  Pages and GitHub Actions builds. Don't reintroduce a shell- or OS-specific step.
- Deployment is Cloudflare Pages (build `npm run build`, output `dist`,
  `NODE_VERSION=22` matching `.nvmrc`); `.github/workflows/ci.yml` only gates PRs
  with `verify` and `build`. Hash routing needs no rewrite rules. The host origin
  is effectively permanent — `localStorage` data and the installed PWA are bound
  to it.
- PWA icons are generated by `scripts/make-icons.mjs` and are safe to commit;
  `npm run build` regenerates them automatically, and a clean checkout builds
  without them. Run `npm run icons` explicitly for a dev-only setup. The artwork
  itself lives in `scripts/icon-art.mjs` and is shared with
  `scripts/make-mobile-icons.mjs`, so never edit the generated `assets/*.png` or
  `android/app/src/main/res/**` by hand — regenerate instead.
- **The download packs reuse the web build.** `desktop/` is an Electron shell
  that packages `dist/` as `resources/app-dist` and serves it over the privileged
  `app://minhero` scheme (Chromium refuses ES modules over `file://`); Android is
  a Capacitor project (`npm run android:sync` copies `dist/` into
  `android/app/src/main/assets/public`). Both must stay static and offline, and a
  pack must never be built from a stale `dist` — both npm scripts run `build`
  first (the desktop one via `prepare-app`, which refuses an empty `dist`).
- App versions come from the root `package.json` only: `prepare-app` copies it
  into `desktop/package.json`, and `android/app/build.gradle` reads it for
  `versionName`/`versionCode`. Bump `npm version` and nothing else.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds the `.exe`/`.apk` on a `v*` tag and
  attaches them to the release. The APK needs the four `ANDROID_*` signing
  secrets (keystore base64, store password, alias, key password); local builds
  read `android/key.properties`, which is git-ignored. Never commit a keystore —
  Android only accepts updates signed with the same key. macOS signing is not
  configured, so only Windows and Android artifacts are produced.
- Never delete and re-push a tag that already has a release: GitHub detaches the
  release and turns it into a draft (it keeps `tag_name` but disappears from the
  Releases list). Move a bad tag by editing the release
  (`gh release edit <tag> --draft=false`) or by bumping the version instead.
- Share links come from `shareBaseUrl()` (`src/core/share.ts`), which honours
  `VITE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` at build time because the packs serve the app from a local
  origin (`app://minhero/`, `https://localhost/`). Keep new link building behind
  that helper.
- The decompiled ToyChestGames source (`minhero-towerofsages-main/`) is local-only
  and gitignored. Derived factual data is committed under
  `src/packs/minhero/data/`; derived art is committed under `public/assets/`
  (see `public/assets/ATTRIBUTION.md`). Never ship the raw source tree.
- Move records carry `icon` (the source `moveIcon_*` name). Resolve it with
  `moveIconPath`; never build `./assets/...` URLs by hand.
- Asset paths in the manifest are relative (`./assets/...`) on purpose, matching
  the type icons so `base: './'` works on a subpath, `file://` and the PWA.
- **Paths injected into CSS custom properties must go through `cssUrl()`**
  (`src/ui/dom.ts`). A relative `url()` inside a custom property resolves against
  the stylesheet that *consumes* it, so in a build (`/assets/index-*.css`)
  `./assets/ui/x.png` becomes `/assets/assets/ui/x.png` and 404s; dev only looks
  right because the stylesheet sits in `/src/`. `cssUrl()` resolves against
  `document.baseURI` first, which keeps subpath/`file://` support. Attribute
  paths (`<img src>`, `background-image` set as a property) are fine as-is.

## Architecture

Small layers, no component tree, no react-style diffing:

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `src/main.ts` | Builds the shell (header, `<main id="view">`, footer, bottom tabs), registers routes, keeps tab highlighting in sync, and subscribes the store to `refresh()`. |
| `src/router.ts` | Hash router: `route(name, view)`, `startRouting(mount, listener)`, `navigate(path)`, `refresh()`, `currentRoute()`. `View` receives `(params, query)`. |
| `src/core/store.ts` | Versioned localStorage state (`mhc:v1`): team/enemy slots, slot builds, build library, saved teams, settings. Mutations persist and notify subscribers. |
| `src/core/types.ts` | Shared stats/build/saved-team/app-state types, independent of the UI. |
| `src/packs/minhero/rules.ts` | Min Hero type metadata and rules (14 types with icons, team size, level/point/tree constants, multipliers). |
| `src/packs/minhero/data.ts` | Typed accessors and id maps for the generated JSON (minions, families, trees, moves, chart, meta). |
| `src/packs/minhero/data/*.json` | Generated data. Do not hand-edit; regenerate with `npm run data:import`. |
| `src/packs/minhero/assets.ts` | Typed accessors for the generated art manifest (`minionSpritePath`, `moveIconPath`, `uiAsset`). |
| `scripts/import-game-data.mjs` | Dev-time ActionScript parser/evaluator that writes the data pack. Never runs at runtime. |
| `scripts/import-assets.mjs` | Dev-time copier that writes `public/assets/**` and `data/assets.json` under stable, app-friendly names. |
| `scripts/check-assets.mjs` | Verifies every manifest path exists under `public/assets` (works on a fresh clone). |
| `scripts/icon-art.mjs` | Dependency-free PNG painter shared by the PWA icons and the mobile pack art. |
| `scripts/make-mobile-icons.mjs` | Writes `assets/icon-*.png` / `assets/splash.png`; `@capacitor/assets` turns them into `android/.../res/**`. |
| `scripts/build-android.mjs` | Runs `gradlew assembleRelease` (finding the SDK via env or `local.properties`) and copies the APK to `release/`. |
| `capacitor.config.json` | Android app id `com.cyberaxies.minherocalc`, `webDir: dist`, `androidScheme: https` (stable `https://localhost` origin for localStorage). |
| `desktop/main.cjs` | Electron main process: `app://` protocol over `dist`, external-link guard, and the `--smoke` boot assertion. |
| `desktop/electron-builder.yml` | NSIS installer + portable `.exe` targets; ships `dist/` as `resources/app-dist`. |
| `src/packs/minhero/pack.ts` | The active game pack, combining rules and generated data. |
| `src/core/rational.ts` | Exact rational arithmetic and formatting helpers used by all type math. |
| `src/core/typechart.ts` | Chart lookup, exact effectiveness/STAB, ratings, best attack, and defensive profiles. |
| `src/core/builds.ts` | 17-point build planner: specialization, row gates, dependency gates, secondary-tree gate, purchases, refunds, validation, and node statuses. |
| `src/core/gems.ts` | Gem maths from `OwnedGem.as`: tier base values, quality rolls, loadout bonuses, effective stats and sanitising. |
| `src/core/coverage.ts` | Offense/defense coverage over the real 102-minion roster, custom enemy matchups, and unique type combinations. |
| `src/core/indexes.ts` | Reverse index built once: move → learning minions with the source (`starting`, `specialization`, `tree`). |
| `src/core/filters.ts` | Query parser/matcher for both browsers (`type:fire`, `!type:water`, `attack>=200`, `stage:2`, `learns:flurry`) plus chip-state merging and active counts. |
| `src/core/share.ts` | Base64url team/build links with validation and unknown-id sanitization. |
| `src/core/format.ts` | Shared stat, rating, target, effect, and move-summary formatters. |
| `src/style.css` | All component/page CSS, imported once from `main.ts` after the token and font layers. |
| `src/styles/tokens.css` | Design tokens (palette, radii, shadows, fonts, texture hooks). Themes override under `:root[data-theme]`. |
| `src/styles/fonts.css` | `@font-face` for BurbinCasual, imported through Vite so the URL is hashed and base-relative. |
| `src/ui/theme.ts` | Theme registry + `applyTheme()`: sets `data-theme` and injects art-based `--texture-*` variables. |
| `src/ui/views.ts` | Stable route-export barrel; re-exports the route views from `pages.ts`. |
| `src/ui/pages.ts` | Route implementations for team, roster, minion detail, chart, and saved setups. |
| `src/ui/moveSearch.ts` | `#/moves` browser (obtainable moves by default) and `#/move/:id` detail with description, move line and learners. |
| `src/ui/filterState.ts` | Per-view filter state that survives full re-renders (module-level slots). |
| `src/ui/plannerState.ts` | Active skill-tree tab per minion, so investing a point does not jump back to tree 1. |
| `src/ui/components/filterBar.ts` | Shared search/type-chip/advanced controls; mutates the slot state and calls back on every edit. |
| `src/ui/actions.ts` | Store-facing UI actions: slot picks, builds, drafts, saved teams, imports, and share loading. |
| `src/ui/components/buildPlanner.ts` | Interactive 3×4×3 tree planner: one tree at a time with arrow/dot navigation, specialization, point meters, and node statuses. |
| `src/ui/components/moveTooltip.ts` | Shared move-description tooltip (hover/focus on desktop, tap to pin on touch; closes on outside tap, Escape, scroll). |
| `src/ui/components/gemPanel.ts` | Gem sockets (usable + locked), local gem editor with tier/quality sliders, and loadout summaries. |
| `src/ui/components/coverage.ts` | Offense, defense, and custom matchup panels. |
| `src/ui/components/minionPicker.ts` | Searchable type-filtered roster picker dialog. |
| `src/ui/components/moveCard.ts` | Collapsible move card (icon, type chip, combat values). |
| `src/ui/components/moveIcon.ts` | Game move icon ringed with its type colour, with a type-icon fallback; sizes `xs`–`lg`. |
| `src/ui/components/dialog.ts` | Modal, share-link, name prompt, and clipboard helpers. |
| `src/ui/components/minionAvatar.ts` | Sprite + game icon-frame avatar (with initials fallback); `portrait` frame for the detail hero. |
| `src/ui/components/typePill.ts` | Shared type chip; uses the inline `--type-color` custom property. |
| `src/ui/dom.ts` | `h(tag, attrs, ...children)` and `frag(...)` DOM builders, plus `cssUrl()` for manifest paths used in custom properties. |

Contracts that only become visible across files:

- Views are full re-renders, so multi-control filter state lives in
  `ui/filterState.ts`, never inside a view. Typing and chips re-run matching and
  sorting in place (no router round-trip), which keeps focus and `<details>`
  state intact. Free text, chips and the advanced panel all merge into one
  `ParsedQuery` via `mergeFilter()`; add new fields there, not in the views.
- **`View` returns `Node | null`**; `null`/`undefined` render nothing but the route
  still counts as active. The optional `URLSearchParams` is parsed from the part of
  the hash after `?`, e.g. `#/minion/domisteam?build=...`.
- **Hash routing is deliberate, not legacy.** `base: './'` plus `#/name/param` keeps
  the build working from `file://`, a GitHub Pages subpath, and an installed PWA,
  and keeps deep links alive after "Add to Home Screen". Do not switch to the
  History API. Unknown routes silently fall back to `team`.
- **`h()` only calls `setAttribute`** — no event handlers, no property assignment
  (`value`, `checked` won't work as objects), and `style` must be a full CSS string.
  Attach listeners to the returned element afterwards.
- Each render sets `document.documentElement.dataset.route` to the resolved route
  name and passes it to the `startRouting` listener; `main.ts` uses that to set
  `aria-current="page"` on the active tab. Adding a tab means adding an entry to
  `TABS` **and** a matching `route(...)` registration. The detail routes
  `minion` and `move` highlight `minions` and `moves` respectively.

## Domain rules to keep consistent

- 14 elements are defined as `TYPES` in `src/packs/minhero/rules.ts` with
  Pokémon-style hex colours. Type metadata belongs in the pack alongside the
  14×14 chart; don't spread it to further files.
- Effectiveness is **multiplicative**: weak ×1.5, resist ×2/3, same-type attack
  bonus ×1.1. Dual types multiply, so doubly weak = 2.25×, weak + resist = exactly
  neutral (1.0), and doubly resistant = 4/9. Use exact rational math in the engine
  rather than floating-point products. UI copy already states these numbers — keep
  new code and text in agreement.
- Fixed game facts: 5 team slots, 14 types, 102 minions across 54 families, 159
  referenced trees, 888 defined moves (893 slots declared by the source; ids
  135–139 are undocumented/glitched), and 785 referenced moves. These counts live in
  `meta.json` and the data tests, not in UI copy.
- Trees are 3 columns × 4 rows and are stored column-major (`col * 4 + row`); each
  point buys the next move id in a node. Only nodes flagged `requiresPreviousRow`
  have the extra same-column dependency; do not apply it universally.
- Gems: tier T grants `ceil(base(T) * quality / 100)` where `base(1) = 3` and
  `base(T) = 2 + T(T+1)/2`; quality is 60–140% (source rolls 1 ± 0.4). Loadouts
  are keyed by minion id in `AppState.loadouts` and add flat points on top of L60
  stats. Locked sockets come from `minion.gems.locked` and stay disabled.
- Version 1.0 is feature-complete: asset pipeline, sprite and move-icon art, the
  slate/gold theme, the move browser, Showdown-style filters, gem loadouts, and the
  single-tree planner with move tooltips. Treat the current build as the shipping
  baseline and make small, verified adjustments from here.

## Conventions

- Strict TS with flags that change how you write code:
  - `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` — indexed reads and `Map`/array access are
    `T | undefined`. Prefer destructuring defaults (`const [name = DEFAULT_ROUTE, ...params] = segments`)
    over non-null assertions.
  - `verbatimModuleSyntax` — type-only imports must use `import type`.
  - `noUnusedLocals` / `noUnusedParameters` / `noImplicitOverride` /
    `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch` are on; unused parameters need a leading `_`.
  - `resolveJsonModule` is on for the generated data pack; import JSON through
    `src/packs/minhero/data.ts` or `pack.ts` rather than scattering raw JSON imports.
- CSS is one global `src/style.css` imported once from `main.ts`, layered after
  `src/styles/fonts.css` and `src/styles/tokens.css`. Class names are BEM-ish
  (`block__element`, `block--modifier`, e.g. `.app-header__title`,
  `.badge--done`); colours, radii, shadows and typefaces come from `:root`
  custom properties in `tokens.css` — never hard-code a colour in a component.
  Type-specific colours come from the pack and are passed inline.
- The palette follows the game's slate-and-gold menus. BurbinCasual is the
  display face for chrome (titles, tabs, buttons, labels); body copy stays on the
  system stack. A 1.1 theme setting should add a `:root[data-theme='…']` block
  and a `THEMES` entry, then call `applyTheme(name)`.
- Per-element colouring is done by setting a custom property inline
  (`style="--type-color:#..."`) and consuming it in CSS (`.type-pill`), not by
  generating per-type classes.
- Mobile-first: fixed bottom tab bar, `env(safe-area-inset-*)` padding for notched
  devices, and a single `@media (min-width: 720px)` breakpoint that promotes the
  tabs to a static top row. Keep new UI within `.app-main`'s 720px column.
- Everything is precached for offline use (`workbox.globPatterns`); the app must
  never fetch at runtime. Static assets belong in `public/` and are referenced with
  relative paths so `base: './'` keeps working.
- Type icons live in `public/icons/IconType*.png`; `types.json` stores their
  relative paths. Use `typePill(type)` for the standard icon chip, and pass
  `typePill(type, true)` only where the visible label is needed.
- The data pack is generated, not hand-written. Edit
  `scripts/import-game-data.mjs`, run `npm run data:import`, then
  `npm run data:check`. Keep the raw decompiled source and assets out of the
  repository.
